description: Open database of about 35,000 grid-scale power plants in 167 countries with location, capacity, primary fuel, owner and reported or estimated generation. Shown here: all nuclear plants and all other plants of 50 MW or more.

coverage.geographic: Global (167 countries); completeness varies strongly by country and is weakest for small renewable plants and for China.
coverage.temporal: Static snapshot: version 1.3.0, released June 2021, with capacity data mostly from 2017–2019 and generation up to 2019.

updateCadence.upstream: Not maintained: WRI states there are no planned updates (last release v1.3.0, 2021)

license.notes: Stated in the repository README and on the WRI dataset page. Suggested citation: Global Energy Observatory, Google, KTH Royal Institute of Technology in Stockholm, Enipedia, World Resources Institute. 2018. Global Power Plant Database. Published on Resource Watch and Google Earth Engine.

limitations: STATIC AND AGEING: the database was last updated in 2021 and is no longer maintained by WRI. Plants commissioned since then are missing, and plants that have since closed (for example all German nuclear plants) are still listed as if operating.
Display filter applied by this application: nuclear plants of any size are shown, every other fuel only from 50 MW capacity upwards (about 10,700 of 34,936 plants).

No operating status is published; capacity, fuel and owner reflect the 'year of capacity data' of each national source (mostly 2017–2019). Owners are organisation names as published and may be outdated.
Locations are of mixed quality (national registries, crowd-sourced GEODB, manual matching) and can be off by kilometres; some plants are aggregated from unit-level data.
'Estimated generation' values are model outputs by WRI, not measurements; the commissioning year is a capacity-weighted average over units where units differ.
confidenceNotes: No per-record confidence is published. Compiled by WRI from national registries and third-party databases with partly automated matching; treat as an indicative historical inventory, not as current operational status.

retention.note: Reference data: a plant is kept for as long as the published file lists it.
